title: Modern C# 12, 13 & 14 Deep-Dive
exp: Stay current on modern C# enhancements: Primary Constructors, Collection Expressions, ref struct generic parameters, System.Threading.Lock, and field keyword.
pts: **Primary Constructors:** syntax for classes/structs (`public class OrderService(IDbContext db)`).
**`System.Threading.Lock`** (.NET 9+): dedicated lock object providing faster OS primitives than `object` locking.
**`field` contextual keyword** (C# 13/14): auto-property backed field access inside property getters/setters.
**Params Collections:** `void Log(params ReadOnlySpan<string> msgs)` avoiding array allocations.
pr: Refactor a legacy C# service to use Primary Constructors & Collection Expressions

r: Deep mechanics of Modern C# 12, 13 & 14 Deep-Dive under concurrent execution.
Always design for idempotency, cancellation propagation, and thread safety.
Memory allocation spikes or CPU bound thread starvation.
Use profiling tools to measure actual baseline allocation before optimizing.
Balancing developer velocity with operational maintenance complexity.
Favor simple, well-tested modular architectures over premature complexity.

qa.q: What are the advantages of using System.Threading.Lock over locking on object in .NET 9+?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** System.Threading.Lock provides a dedicated, lightweight OS synchronization primitive designed specifically for thread locking, avoiding the memory footprint of a full System.Object header and reducing lock contention overhead.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** C# compiler synthesizes an IAsyncStateMachine struct. Awaiting incomplete tasks yields control to the caller; thread pool threads resume via TaskScheduler/SynchronizationContext.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Blocking async code with .Result or .Wait() on single-threaded synchronization contexts leads to deadlocks and thread pool starvation.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Async preserves thread pool scalability for I/O operations, but introduces state machine allocations and complex exception bubbling.

qa.q: How do collection expressions and the spread operator improve both syntax and allocation efficiency?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Collection expressions [...] provide a unified syntax for arrays, Span<T>, List<T>, and ImmutableCollections. The compiler optimizes allocation by pre-calculating capacity when combining arrays via spread [..a, ..b].

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** T-SQL engine parses, compiles into execution plans, caches them in the plan cache, and executes via the storage engine (buffer pool & latching).

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Parameter sniffing and missing stats cause sub-optimal plan compilation, resulting in full table scans and high CPU.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Parameterization improves plan reuse, but recompile hints (OPTION RECOMPILE) may be needed for skewed data distributions.
